I have been farming this land in Quzhou for fifty years. My back is not what it was, some of my sons and daughters earn wages in the city now, so I have less hands than before. But I know this land. I will manage it the way I know works.

My 9 mu — I will put 6 mu in wheat-maize rotation as always, and the other 3 mu in cotton. Cotton is more work but the price is better and I have grown it for decades.

For wheat this winter, I will plant the improved variety I buy from the township seed station — the same kind I have used for several years now, good germination, decent yield. I put down compound fertilizer as base before sowing, then top-dress with urea at jointing. I always use a good amount — maybe 50 jin of urea per mu across the season plus base, my father did this too. I will irrigate at pre-winter, jointing, and heading — three times with my well pump. Two or three pesticide sprays for aphids and rust. Rotary tillage before planting after maize harvest.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed — that has been standard for many years now, the yield is much better than the old varieties. I apply less fertilizer than wheat, one or two irrigations if July rains fail, one or two pesticide sprays. I direct seed into the wheat stubble with minimal tillage.

For cotton on my 3 mu, I use the Bt variety — it reduced my bollworm spraying a lot compared to the old days. But I still need to spray for aphids and spider mites, probably five or six times through the season. Cotton needs more water and more phosphorus and potash. I plough before planting in late April.
